mechanism_narrative: When the monthly FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, it anticipates a tightening bias that reduces discounting of future earnings, thereby pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the subsequent month
failure_condition: Over 60-day walk-forward window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite FEDFUNDS increases >0.25pp, or the SPX 5-day returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.3% for two consecutive months predicts a disinflationary environment that reduces rate-cut expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL declines ≥0.3% for two months, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by other proxies (GDPC1, FEDFUNDS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of more than 50,000 jobs in a month coincides with corporate hiring optimism and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a month
failure_condition: In expansionary regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent after controlling for GDPC1 and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDPC1 (nominal private demand) and HOUST (retail sales) show consecutive monthly increases above their prior month's levels, it signals resilient demand momentum that produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase in the same month relative to prior month
failure_condition: In robust demand regimes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive after controlling for FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 0.5% above the prior month, accompanied by a decline in RSAFS (retail sales), predicts a supply-side imbalance that pushes S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥0.5% while RSAFS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In supply-imbalance regimes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.05), or the effect is mediated by FEDFUNDS changes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.2 percentage points over the next three months, it indicates weaker wage growth expectations and tends to precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp over next 3 months
failure_condition: In wage moderation regimes, the 5-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.05), or the effect persists only in contractionary macro environments.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% for two consecutive months signals accommodative policy and tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In prolonged low-rate regimes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by alternative proxies (CPIAUCSL, GDPC1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in PAYEMS exceeding 70,000 jobs and a simultaneous decline in UNRATE by at least 0.1 percentage points suggest labor market expansion without wage pressure, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >70,000 while UNRATE decreases by ≥0.1pp in the same month
regime_hint: labor market expansion with soft wage growth
failure_condition: In such regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive after controlling for FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (F-test p > 0.05).
